newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SEVENTH TOUR WIN FOR WESTERN SAMOA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SEVENTH TOUR WIN FOR WESTERN SAMOA.

text.p: Western Samoa chalked up their seventh victory in 10 games on their British tour with a 33-20 win over a selection from the Leicester and Northampton clubs on Wednesday.

In their penultimate game, the Samoans scored five tries to two and although the home side came back from 20-6 down at halftime to get within three points at 20-23, the tourists thoroughly deserved their win in the end.

Their tries came from number eight Isaac Feaunati, centre Terry Fanolua, captain Pat Lam and the two replacements -- Sene Ta'ala and Filipo Toala. Fly-half Fa'avaivai Tanoai converted just one of the tries and kicked two penalties.
The home side's tries came from a penalty try for a collapsed scrum and lock forward John Hearn, with Leicester's fly-half Niall Malone kicking two conversions and two penalties.
The match got off to a low-key start and was level at 3-3 after 24 minutes before the Samoans scored two tries in the space of six minutes to go 13-3 ahead.
A Malone penalty made it 6-13, but the Samoans scored a third try right on half-time to turn around 13 points ahead.

The home side then scored two tries in the opening 15 minutes of the second half either side of a penalty by the Samoans to make the score 20-23 and, although their forwards had some good spells, they could not find a way through to get on terms.
